page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6.26xlarge is a general-purpose instance hosted on the KVM hypervisor. The platform is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. It provides 104 dedicated vCPUs along with 384 GB of system memory, which establishes a balanced ratio of approximately 3.69 GB of memory per core. The instance lacks integrated GPU acceleration, targeting standard non-accelerated compute environments.

Network infrastructure for this instance offers a baseline bandwidth of 25 Gbps, supporting moderate-to-high inter-node data exchange in distributed environments. The server has no integrated local storage, requiring persistent data and operating system installations to rely entirely on external network-attached cloud disks. Furthermore, zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

Because the server relies on dedicated CPU resources without burst mechanisms, it delivers predictable multi-core throughput suitable for horizontally scaled or dense container environments. It is engineered for enterprise-grade backend systems, multi-threaded application servers, distributed cache nodes, and data batch processing workloads that require a massive core footprint paired with balanced system memory.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6.26xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by the KVM hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The configuration supplies 104 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs and 384 GB of memory, equating to 3.69 GB per core. The instance has no local storage volumes, necessitating the use of remote cloud block storage for persistent filesystem needs. Network capabilities include a 25 Gbps baseline bandwidth, providing capacity for intra-cluster traffic and external data transfers. The instance includes zero GPUs and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Designed for high-concurrency tasks requiring substantial thread parallelization and balanced memory allocation, the ecs.g6.26xlarge fits enterprise web application servers, container hosting clusters, continuous integration systems, and medium-scale database infrastructure.
